messages.text: 'State of the Game' report finds most English clubs living on financial brink

metadata.summary: The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has produced a 'State of the Game' report, which has taken a forensic look at English football over the past 18 months, concluding that the game's finances are dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster.
metadata.content: 'State of the Game': Independent Football Regulator's report finds most English clubs living on financial brink | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content 'State of the Game': Independent Football Regulator's report finds most English clubs living on financial brink The Independent Football Regulator published its draft ‘State of the Game’ report on Tuesday, which found that while English football generated £9bn in revenue last season, 94 per cent of clubs in the top five divisions were loss-making Geraint Hughes Sports News Correspondent Tuesday 13 October 2026 17:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News reporter Geraint Hughes explains the Independent Football Regulator's 'State of the Game' report, which explores how most English clubs are living on the brink of financial ruin The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has produced a 'State of the Game' report, which has taken a forensic look at English football over the past 18 months, concluding that the game's finances are dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster. The IFR added that interest and investment from around the world continues to grow within English football, but the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform. metadata.summary: Alexander Zverev celebrated becoming the year-end No 1 with a 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) victory over Alexander Bublik to reach the quarter-finals at the Shanghai Masters.
metadata.content: Shanghai Masters: Alexander Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with win over Alexander Bublik as Katie Boulter bows out of Wuhan Open | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Shanghai Masters: Alexander Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with win over Alexander Bublik as Katie Boulter bows out of Wuhan Open Alexander Zverev struggles with ankle issues but does enough to reach his 40th Masters 1000 quarter-final of his career in China; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports Tuesday 13 October 2026 15:04, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Bublik and Alexander Zverev starred in the point of the week at the Shanghai Open! Alexander Zverev celebrated becoming the year-end No 1 with a 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) victory over Alexander Bublik to reach the quarter-finals at the Shanghai Masters. Zverev, who won the French Open and US Open this year, never looked 100 per cent comfortable, and admitted his "ankle was acting up" following his win. The top seed will take on ninth seed Alex de Minaur next after the Australian produced one of his best performances of the year to beat Karen Khachanov in straight sets 6-3 6-4 to advance. messages.text: Iraola has ‘100 per cent’ trust in Wirtz and Barcola

metadata.summary: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has “100 per cent” trust in Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola after the two £100m-plus signings came in for criticism.
metadata.content: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool boss has ‘100 per cent’ trust in Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Andoni Iraola: Liverpool boss has ‘100 per cent’ trust in Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola Liverpool big-money signings Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola have come under criticism; Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher has called for Wirtz to be dropped after another poor showing in the loss to Manchester City; Reds boss Andoni Iraola: "Barcola and Flo are players I trust 100 per cent" Tuesday 13 October 2026 19:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola backs Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to perform at a 'top level' for Liverpool this season Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has “100 per cent” trust in Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola after the two £100m-plus signings came in for criticism. Wirtz has had the benefit of a full season already with the club but has yet to deliver on his £116m price tag, and in Sunday's home loss to Manchester City he struggled to exert any influence on the game even when his side were in the ascendancy. Barcola, who joined from PSG in a £123m deal, can be given more leeway after arriving late in this summer's transfer window, but he looked short of confidence and has yet to properly contribute in six appearances. messages.text: A PL giant to fall? Newly-promoted clubs changing relegation equation

metadata.summary: Hull, Coventry and Ipswich have already collected 24 points between them after six games, so the conversation is starting to shift from pre-season vibes on whether all three newly-promoted clubs will be relegated to which established Premier League names could be in the scrap for survival.
metadata.content: A Premier League giant to fall? Hull, Ipswich and Coventry are changing the relegation equation this season | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis A Premier League giant to fall? Hull, Ipswich and Coventry are changing the relegation equation this season Hull City, Ipswich Town and Coventry City are all clear of the Premier League relegation zone after six games; does this put a supposedly safe mid-table club or a big-name team in genuine danger of relegation to the Championship this season? Tuesday 13 October 2026 15:38, UK Image: Premier League relegation picture: Will Ipswich, Coventry and Hull all survive? Hull, Coventry and Ipswich have already collected 24 points between them after six games, so the conversation is starting to shift from pre-season vibes on whether all three newly-promoted clubs will be relegated to which established Premier League names could be in the scrap for survival. The Premier League's newly-promoted sides have often struggled to bridge the gap, with two consecutive seasons in 2023/24 and 2024/25 seeing all three newcomers relegated before Leeds and Sunderland helped buck that trend last season. messages.text: Rowley appointed new Tigers head coach

metadata.summary: Paul Rowley has been confirmed as the new Castleford Tigers head coach after signing a three-year deal with the club.
metadata.content: Paul Rowley: Castleford Tigers appoint former St Helens boss as head coach on three-year deal after departure of Ryan Carr | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Paul Rowley: Castleford Tigers appoint former St Helens boss as head coach on three-year deal after departure of Ryan Carr Castleford Tigers have appointed Paul Rowley as their head coach on a three-year contract with the club only being kept off the bottom of Super League by Bradford Bulls last season Tuesday 13 October 2026 11:06, UK Image: Paul Rowley has been confirmed as the new Castleford Tigers head coach Paul Rowley has been confirmed as the new Castleford Tigers head coach after signing a three-year deal with the club. Rowley left St Helens in July with the club on their way to missing out on the Super League play-offs for the first time, having previously been in charge of Salford prior to the club's financial collapse in 2025. He takes over at the Tigers following the departure of Australian Ryan Carr for personal reasons two months ago.
